text:
as u watch people around u navigate life, over years and decades, u will see that attitude really does overpower everything

especially setbacks.

on one hand this is a frighteningly cliche observation; yet at the same time, like Munger's "show me the incentive and I'll show you the outcome," there are principles where the order of magnitude matters

i.e. you recognize it as a truth, but the all-pervading importance of it has to be further emphasized

on good vs bad attitudes...

GOOD: 

a person's attitude runs extremely deep. I don't think its something that can be altered.

this is one of those aspects of human nature, a mystery, where we'll land rockets upside-down on the sun before we understand how attitudes are hardwired

when you see someone with an exceptional attitude face adversity, its like an instinctual reaction: 

"nothing but a setback."

everything falls into that category. its all nothing but a setback. I'm always awestruck when I see it which is why this is my 500th tweet on attitude.

everything to them is an opportunity to improve, a test, a chance to prove themselves...everything is met with the question "what can I learn from this?" 

the belief that there are no losses, only lessons

u never see a person with a winning attitude complain...they accept constraints, and they find ways to win within them.

the book "The Diving Bell and the Butterfly" to me is the embodiment of an exceptional attitude, just the level of sheer willpower and determination required to make that happen.

BAD:

I won't dwell too much on bad attitudes because its pointless. a bad attitude can't be altered, nor does it have any interest in being altered. it was only in the last 3-6 months that I accepted this.

a bad attitude is the envious, victim mentality-type, always blaming and making excuses, always wallowing or attacking others.

a change in attitude would mean taking ownership of all one's flaws and shortcomings and failures. that means pain. its easier to keep blaming it all on the world.

once u see that someone is wired this way, just keep moving. u can go around trying to save people all u want -- u will eventually learn that some ppl have no interest in being saved.

THE PATH FORWARD

u have to take people as they come, one by one. 

they are unpredictable. rich, poor, where they grew up, what they do, where they went to school, none of that matters...there is zero correlation between attitude and anything else.

all I've learned is to recognize and avoid bad attitudes, they will bring u down. whereas good attitudes, they fill u with energy rather than drain u....find these people and surround yourself with them, they will bring u higher.

the difference between a good attitude and a truly amazing attitude only makes itself clear in the face of a setback.

thats when u will really see everything written here in action. just like Plutarch wrote, about how the shoe shapes itself to the foot -- this is exactly how life is shaped by a person who has an exceptional attitude.

quotedTweet.text:
one of the best quotes on attitude is an analogy from 2000 years ago, in Plutarch's Moralia, on how temperament dictates circumstance

"Just as the shoe follows the shape of the foot, and not the other way around, so do men's dispositions make their lives like themselves."
